docs.title: bagx
docs.text:
Post-processing analysis engine for ROS2 rosbag data.

Try bagx in your browser — drop a .db3 bag, get a readiness report. No install, and your bag never leaves your machine.

bagx is not a replacement for ros2 bag. ros2 bag handles recording & playback (I/O). bagx handles evaluation, understanding & comparison (Analysis).

docs.title: What can you do with bagx?
docs.text:
# Score a bag's sensor quality
bagx eval recording.db3
bagx rules list
bagx eval recording.db3 --rules warehouse_bot

# Compare two runs
bagx compare run_A.db3 run_B.db3

# Check time sync between sensors
bagx sync recording.db3 /camera /lidar

# Find sensor anomalies
bagx anomaly recording.db3

# Export for ML pipelines
bagx export recording.db3 --ai --format parquet

# Batch-evaluate a dataset
bagx batch eval ./recordings/*.db3 --csv summary.csv

# Re-run a benchmark suite on curated public/private bags
bagx benchmark benchmarks/open_data_suite.json
bagx benchmark benchmarks/non_slam_suite.json

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to bagx are documented here. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and versions follow the policy in Versioning and compatibility.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• bagx tf: TF tree validation (multiple parents, cycles, disconnected trees, transforms on both /tf and /tf_static, pauses and early stops, zero or regressing stamps, clock mismatches between topics, sensor frame_ids missing from the tree, --require-frames, --fail-on). The same checks run inside bagx eval (tf.* findings, TF: recommendations, report.tf) and as the MCP tool check_tf. They do not change scores.
  • Message content checks in bagx eval (msg.* findings, Data: recommendations): scans with no or few valid ranges, invalid scan config, beam count changes, uncalibrated or zero-size camera_info, camera_info vs image size mismatch, truncated images, resolution or encoding changes, joint_states shared by publishers with different joint sets, name/position length mismatch, NaN joints, and empty frame_id. These do not change scores.
  • CDR fallback parsers (no ROS needed) for sensor_msgs LaserScan, CameraInfo, Image, CompressedImage and JointState.
  • Header-stamp matched pipeline latency: when a stage's output carries its input's stamp, latency is measured exactly per message and reported with (header-stamp matched).
  • Scoreboard manifest integrity: provenance, availability, bag fingerprints and scripts/generate_scoreboard.py --check.
  • CI runs the test suite on ROS 2 Humble and Jazzy, including rosbag2_py vs SQLite backend parity tests.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Report schema_version 1.3.0 → 1.4.0. This is additive: eval JSON gains tf and new finding categories tf_tree and message_content.
  • eval.py is split into eval_topics, eval_workflow, eval_latency and eval_domains. This is a code move with no behavior change, and the old bagx.eval imports still work.
  • Scoreboard: TurtleBot3 Walker and Franka Panda rows are marked source_unavailable; r2b rows point at NVIDIA NGC. Livox MID-360 is pinned to the AIST Zenodo bag (the same bag the 0.4.0 score came from) and NTU VIRAL to eee_03 on DR-NTU. Newer College (download needs a request form) is unscored until a sequence is pinned. Ouster OS0-32 is source_unavailable, because its recording was never tied to a public file. Every available public bag is rescored after the sync fix below, and rows scored on unreleased code record bagx_version as X.Y.Z+dev.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Sync score (bagx eval, all SLAM / Autoware / perception bags with two or more sensor streams): each pair walked whichever topic sorted first by name and took the nearest message on the other. For a dense/sparse pair such as 200 Hz IMU ↔ 10 Hz LiDAR this measured a quarter of the LiDAR period (~25 ms) however well the streams were aligned, and raised a false "enable per-point deskew" warning. The pair now walks the sparser topic, so sync scores rise on bags with mixed rates (Livox MID-360 70 → 100, Autoware bag4 67.7 → 87.4) and the tuned FAST-LIO comment about deskew disappears where it was spurious. bagx scenario sync_degraded uses the same rule.
  • sensor_msgs Temperature, MagneticField, FluidPressure, RelativeHumidity, Illuminance and BatteryState topics no longer count as sync candidates because their name contains imu or camera (e.g. /imu/temperature was paired with a camera on NTU VIRAL).
  • NavSatFix CDR parser misread status / service unless len(frame_id) + 1 was a multiple of 4 (e.g. gnss_link), which skewed the GNSS fix rate on the SQLite fallback.
  • On ROS 2 Jazzy every rclpy-decoded message failed to convert (_check_fields slot), so the ROS backend silently fell back to the CDR parser and custom message types lost their content.
  • pip install bagx[mcp] pulled mcp 2.x, which broke bagx mcp; mcp is now <2.
  • pyarrow 26 needs NumPy 2 at import time, so bagx export failed on ROS 2 systems with NumPy 1.x; pyarrow is now <26.
  • Ruff rule selection is pinned, so CI no longer breaks when ruff changes its defaults.

docs.text:
bagx works with or without ROS:

  • With ROS2: Full message deserialization via rosbag2_py
  • Without ROS2: .db3 files are read via SQLite with built-in CDR parsers for common types (NavSatFix, Imu, PoseStamped, Odometry, PointCloud2, TFMessage)

docs.title: Public Dataset Scoreboard
docs.text:
bagx scores public rosbag datasets with a single command (bagx eval). This page is generated from benchmarks/scoreboard.json so scores stay reproducible across releases.

Scores are readiness hints, not SLAM trajectory accuracy. They summarize sensor rates, sync, IMU noise, and stack-specific topic coverage (Nav2 / Autoware / MoveIt / perception).

The Data column says where each bag comes from: public rows are scored on the upstream download, sim rows on bags captured with scripts/run_ros_dogfood.py, and unavailable rows are tracked but unscored because the upstream bag can no longer be downloaded.

export BAGX_SCOREBOARD_BAGS=/path/to/bags

docs.title: anomaly — Anomaly Detection
docs.text: Automatically detect anomalies and outliers in sensor data.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx anomaly recording.db3
bagx anomaly recording.db3 --topic /gnss
bagx anomaly recording.db3 --json anomalies.json

docs.title: GNSS
docs.text:
• position_jump: Position change > 50m between consecutive messages
  • fix_drop: Fix status transitions from valid to invalid
  • hdop_spike: HDOP exceeds mean + 3σ

docs.title: IMU
docs.text:
• accel_spike: Acceleration magnitude exceeds mean + 4σ
  • gyro_spike: Gyro rate exceeds mean + 4σ
  • imu_frequency_drop: Message gap > 3× median interval

docs.title: General
docs.text: • rate_gap: Any topic with message gap > 3× median interval

docs.title: Severity levels
docs.text: Level Meaning high Likely sensor failure or data corruption medium Unusual but may be legitimate (e.g., rapid maneuver) low Minor deviation, informational

docs.title: Temporal findings
docs.text:
Each anomaly run also produces a findings array — raw events aggregated into structured Finding objects with time_range (absolute ROS time nanoseconds). GNSS fix-drop events are paired with the next recovery (or the bag end) to form anomaly.gnss.fix_lost.<topic> segments; other event types cluster by (topic, type) within a 30 second window.

Anomaly severities map to finding severities as low → info, medium → warning, high → error.

For CI workflows, prefer bagx eval --include-anomaly so the temporal findings ship alongside the rest of the eval report and can be gated with bagx diff or bagx benchmark. See eval — Temporal findings.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Gathers bag context automatically:
    • Summary (topics, message counts, duration)
    • Quality evaluation (GNSS/IMU/sync scores)
    • First 3 message samples from each topic
  2. Sends the context + your question to the LLM
  3. Returns the LLM's analysis

• Files: Used directly (bag.db3)
  • Directories: Recursively scans for .db3 and .mcap files
  • Globs: Expanded by the shell (*.db3)

docs.title: benchmark — Benchmark Suites
docs.text:
Run a manifest-driven suite of curated bag checks.

This is useful when you want public rosbag datasets and internal gold bags to act like a reproducible regression suite, not ad hoc manual checks.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Run all cases in a suite
bagx benchmark benchmarks/open_data_suite.json
bagx benchmark benchmarks/non_slam_suite.json
bagx benchmark warehouse_benchmark.json --rules warehouse_bot

# Export a machine-readable report
bagx benchmark benchmarks/open_data_suite.json --json benchmark-report.json

# Run only selected cases
bagx benchmark benchmarks/open_data_suite.json --case nvidia-r2b-robotarm

# Fail if any referenced bag is missing
bagx benchmark benchmarks/open_data_suite.json --fail-on-missing

docs.title: Manifest format
docs.text:
The manifest is JSON and supports environment-variable expansion in bag_path. It also supports optional rules_path values to apply custom message rules. rules_path can be either a JSON file path or a plugin name.

{
  "suite_name": "open-data-dogfood",
  "rules_path": "warehouse_bot",
  "cases": [
    {
      "name": "nvidia-r2b-galileo2",
      "bag_path": "${BAGX_REALBAGS}/r2b_galileo2",
      "report_type": "eval",
      "expect": {
        "min_overall_score": 90,
        "required_domains": ["Perception"],
        "required_recommendations": [
          "Perception topics detected",
          "Camera calibration topics are recorded"
        ],
        "forbidden_recommendations": ["No GNSS data", "No IMU data"]
      }
    }
  ]
}

The repository ships ready-made suites:

  • benchmarks/open_data_suite.json: public Autoware + NVIDIA bags
  • benchmarks/non_slam_suite.json: perception/manipulation plus optional local Nav2 / MoveIt dogfood bags
  • benchmarks/scoreboard.json: 30 datasets (public + labeled simulator captures) for the Scoreboard page; python scripts/generate_scoreboard.py --check validates it

Regenerate the docs table after scoring local bags:

./scripts/fetch_scoreboard_bags.sh   # Autoware S3 + AutoCore (optional)
export BAGX_SCOREBOARD_BAGS=/path/to/bags
export BAGX_DB3_CACHE=/path/with/free/space
python scripts/generate_scoreboard.py --refresh --write-manifest
python scripts/generate_scoreboard.py

For proprietary stacks, pair a benchmark manifest with a custom rules plugin or file and keep your expectations in required_domains, required_recommendations, and min_topic_rates.

docs.title: Supported expectations
docs.text:
• min_overall_score
  • max_overall_score
  • min_domain_score
  • required_domains
  • required_recommendations
  • forbidden_recommendations
  • expected_findings
  • min_topic_rates
  • required_topics

docs.title: expected_findings
docs.text:
expected_findings checks structured readiness findings by stable id instead of matching human-facing recommendation text. See eval — Structured findings for the available ids and severity policy.

{
  "expect": {
    "expected_findings": [
      {
        "id": "nav2.detected",
        "severity": "info",
        "domain": "nav2",
        "category": "domain_detection"
      }
    ]
  }
}

Each item can be either a bare string (id only) or an object. When an object is given, severity, domain, category, and affected_topics are checked individually and produce separate expected_finding_* sub-checks in the report.

For temporal findings (with a time_range), an time_range_overlap constraint scopes the match to a window of the bag — pass when the finding's time_range overlaps the window:

{
  "id": "anomaly.gnss.fix_lost.gnss",
  "time_range_overlap": {"start_ns": 120000000000, "end_ns": 145000000000}
}

Useful for "GNSS must be lost only during the parked phase" style expectations. Requires the eval report to include temporal findings — run bagx eval --include-anomaly upstream.

docs.title: forbidden_findings
docs.text:
The inverse of expected_findings — fail when listed ids appear. Each item can be either a bare string (id only) or an object with a severity_min scope:

{
  "expect": {
    "forbidden_findings": [
      "nav2.missing_global_plan",
      {"id": "sync.delay.high", "severity_min": "error"}
    ]
  }
}

With severity_min, the finding is only forbidden when its severity is at or above the threshold — letting an info-level appearance through while gating on the worse cases.

forbidden_findings also accepts time_range_overlap (same shape as in expected_findings). Both qualifiers compose: the rule fires only when a matching finding has severity ≥ severity_min and overlaps the constraint window — useful for "no fix-lost during autonomy phase".

docs.title: max_severity
docs.text:
A per-category ceiling. Any finding whose severity exceeds the ceiling fails its case:

{
  "expect": {
    "max_severity": {
      "sensor_quality": "warning",
      "topic_presence": "info"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: --exit-on
docs.text: bagx benchmark suite.json --exit-on warning returns a non-zero exit code when any case's worst finding severity reaches the threshold. Use this together with the case-level passed/failed status to gate CI on both manifest expectations and structural severity.

docs.title: JSON contract
docs.text:
Benchmark JSON reports (schema_version 1.3.0+) include:

  • schema_version
  • report_type
  • bagx_version
  • worst_severity at suite level and on each case
  • finding_ids for each evaluated case

This makes it practical to gate regressions in CI or compare reports across releases.

docs.title: compare — Bag Comparison
docs.text: Compare quality metrics of two bag files side-by-side.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx compare A.db3 B.db3
bagx compare A.db3 B.db3 --json diff.json

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
For each metric, shows:

  • A value and B value
  • Diff (absolute and percentage)
  • Verdict: improved, degraded, or unchanged (threshold: 1%)

Determines an overall winner (A, B, or tie) based on the count of improved vs degraded metrics.

docs.title: custom-rules — Extending bagx for Custom Message Stacks
docs.text:
If your robot uses custom messages, bagx can still evaluate the bag without decoding those payloads.

The custom rule engine works on:

  • topic names
  • topic types
  • message rates
  • timestamp-based latency between topics

This is enough for many internal stacks where the important question is "did we record the right topics at the right rates, and did the control loop react quickly enough?"

Rules can be loaded from:

  • a JSON file path
  • a built-in plugin name such as warehouse_bot
  • a JSON file discovered via BAGX_RULE_PLUGIN_PATH
  • an installed Python package that exposes a bagx.rules entry point

docs.title: CLI usage
docs.text:
bagx rules list
bagx eval warehouse_bag.db3 --rules warehouse_bot
bagx eval warehouse_bag.db3 --rules examples/custom_rules/warehouse_bot.json
bagx benchmark benchmark.json --rules examples/custom_rules/warehouse_bot.json

benchmark also supports rules_path inside the manifest, either at the top level or per case.

Use bagx rules list to see built-in and installed plugins.

Invalid rule files are validated before evaluation. bagx reports all common schema errors it can find, including unknown check kinds, missing selectors, missing thresholds, and non-numeric latency/rate values.

docs.title: Rule format
docs.text:
{
  "domains": [
    {
      "name": "WarehouseBot",
      "min_matches": 2,
      "match_topics": [
        {"name_contains": "wheel_odom", "type_contains": "WheelOdometry"},
        {"name_contains": "controller_cmd", "type_contains": "ControllerCommand"},
        {"name_contains": "mission_path", "type_contains": "MissionPath"}
      ],
      "checks": [
        {
          "kind": "topic_rate",
          "label": "Wheel odometry",
          "selector": {"name_contains": "wheel_odom"},
          "min_rate_hz": 20
        },
        {
          "kind": "topic_exists",
          "label": "Mission result",
          "selector": {"suffix": "/result"}
        },
        {
          "kind": "latency",
          "label": "mission path → controller",
          "input": {"name_contains": "mission_path"},
          "output": {"name_contains": "controller_cmd"},
          "target_ms": 100,
          "max_response_ms": 1000
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

See examples/custom_rules/warehouse_bot.json for a complete example.

docs.title: Plugin distribution
docs.text:
For a team-internal stack, the easiest options are:

  • ship a JSON file and point BAGX_RULE_PLUGIN_PATH at its directory
  • package your rules in Python and expose a bagx.rules entry point that returns a JSON dict, a path, or a CustomRuleSet

That lets other users run:

bagx eval my_bag.db3 --rules your_plugin_name

docs.title: Selector fields
docs.text:
A selector picks which topics a rule applies to. All fields are strings and optional, but a selector with no fields matches nothing.

Field Match against Notes name exact topic name e.g. "/cmd_vel" name_contains substring of topic name most common form prefix topic name prefix suffix topic name suffix type exact message type string e.g. "sensor_msgs/msg/Imu" type_contains substring of message type

Unknown fields raise a schema error at load time.

docs.title: Check schema
docs.text:
Every check requires kind and label. Additional fields depend on kind.

kind Required Optional Purpose topic_exists selector min_samples, severity Topic with at least one message must exist. topic_rate selector, min_rate_hz min_samples, severity Topic must publish above the rate. latency input, output, target_ms max_response_ms, min_samples, severity Median delay from input → output must be ≤ target_ms.

All numeric fields (min_rate_hz, target_ms, max_response_ms) must be numbers; min_samples must be an integer. Invalid documents fail loading with a list of all detected schema errors at once, not one at a time.

docs.title: Per-check severity
docs.text:
Each check accepts an optional severity field that sets the finding severity emitted when the check fails. Defaults to warning. Allowed values are info, warning, error, and critical.

{
  "kind": "topic_rate",
  "label": "Wheel odometry",
  "selector": {"name_contains": "wheel_odom"},
  "min_rate_hz": 20,
  "severity": "error"
}

Use error for checks that must hold for the bag to be usable at all, and keep warning for checks that flag degradation worth investigating. A passing check always emits an info finding regardless of the configured severity.

docs.title: Per-check findings
docs.text:
Each check emits an individual structured finding alongside the per-domain aggregate. Use the per-check ids in expected_findings and forbidden_findings to gate a single check rather than the whole custom domain.

Id format:

custom.<domain_id>.<label_token>.{pass,fail,skipped}
  • <domain_id> is the domain name lowercased with non-alphanumerics replaced.
  • <label_token> is derived from the check label the same way.
  • The last token reflects evaluation outcome: pass, fail, or skipped (latency without enough samples falls into skipped).

The aggregate custom.<domain_id>.evaluated finding is still emitted and remains a good high-level signal; reach for per-check ids when you need to gate individual checks.

docs.title: Typical use cases
docs.text:
• internal vehicle stacks with custom odometry / command / mission messages
  • custom manipulation stacks that expose action results but not MoveIt topics
  • proprietary planners/controllers where topic naming is consistent but message decoding is unavailable

docs.title: diff — Compare two eval reports
docs.text: bagx diff compares two bagx eval --json reports by stable finding id (<domain>.<area>.<qualifier>). Use it in CI to gate PRs against a baseline report from main, or at release time to track readiness regressions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx diff baseline.json current.json
bagx diff baseline.json current.json --format markdown
bagx diff baseline.json current.json --format json --output diff.json
bagx diff baseline.json current.json --exit-on warning
bagx diff baseline.json current.json --include-same

docs.title: Change kinds
docs.text:
Each finding id is classified into one of:

Kind Meaning NEW id only in current — a finding that was not previously emitted GONE id only in baseline — a finding that used to be emitted but no longer is WORSE same id, current severity is higher than baseline BETTER same id, current severity is lower than baseline SAME same id, same severity (hidden by default; use --include-same)

The order of importance in the text rendering is worse → new → gone → better → same.

docs.title: Evidence drift
docs.text: When a finding stays the same severity (SAME), bagx diff still surfaces evidence drift — meaningful changes in numeric observed values within the finding. The default drift threshold is 10% relative change. Non-numeric evidence is reported when the string representation differs.

docs.title: Temporal findings
docs.text:
Findings with a time_range (e.g. anomaly.gnss.fix_lost.<topic> from bagx eval --include-anomaly) are matched segment-by-segment within the same id:

  • Overlapping ranges count as the same segment — a slightly-shifted fix-lost window compares as WORSE / BETTER / SAME rather than GONE+NEW.
  • Disjoint ranges count as different segments — a new fault window shows up as a separate NEW change next to the existing one.

The text and markdown renderers add a segment column / line showing t=<start>-<end>s for the affected window. Pre-1.3 reports without time_range continue to join by id alone, so existing CI pipelines keep working unchanged.

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text:
• text (default): coloured terminal output, one line per change.
  • json: includes the full diff structure plus schema_version, report_type: "diff", and bagx_version, suitable for further machine processing.
  • markdown: a PR-comment friendly table. Use --output diff.md to write directly to a file.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 — no regressions at or above --exit-on severity (default behaviour)
  • 1 — at least one NEW or WORSE finding at the requested severity
  • 2 — invalid CLI arguments (unknown format, unknown severity)

--exit-on warning fails the diff when any NEW or WORSE finding has severity ≥ warning. BETTER and GONE never cause a non-zero exit — they represent improvements.

docs.title: CI example
docs.text:
# baseline is the eval report on main (cached as a GitHub Actions artifact)
bagx eval bag.db3 --json current.json
bagx diff baseline.json current.json --format markdown --output diff.md --exit-on warning

Post diff.md as a PR comment, and let --exit-on warning block the merge when readiness regresses.

A ready-to-use GitHub Actions workflow lives at examples/github_actions/bagx-pr-check.yml. It evaluates the PR bag, restores the previous baseline from cache, runs bagx diff, and posts the markdown result as a sticky PR comment.

docs.title: domain-plugins — Extending Stack Detection
docs.text:
bagx ships built-in domain detection for Nav2, Autoware, MoveIt, Perception, RobotArm, and Control. You can add your own stack without patching bagx by registering a domain plugin.

A domain plugin answers three questions for a bag:

  1. detect — does this bag belong to my stack?
  2. representative_topics — which topics best summarise the stack?
  3. generate_findings — what structured findings should the eval report add?

Plugins are discovered from the bagx.domains Python entry-point group. Built-in domains use the same protocol internally.

docs.title: CLI usage
docs.text:
bagx domains list
bagx eval my_bag.db3 --json report.json

When a plugin matches, eval emits a *.detected finding plus any findings returned by generate_findings.

docs.title: Minimal plugin
docs.text:
from bagx.domain_plugins import SimpleDomainPlugin
from bagx.findings import Evidence, Finding, finding_id

def detect(topic_info: dict) -> bool:
    return any(name.endswith("/rtk/fix") for name in topic_info)

def findings(report) -> list[Finding]:
    return [
        Finding(
            id=finding_id("rtk_gnss", "stack_present"),
            title="RTK GNSS stack detected",
            severity="info",
            category="domain_detection",
            domain="rtk_gnss",
            evidence=[Evidence(metric="domain_detected", observed=True, expected=True)],
            confidence="high",
        )
    ]

plugin = SimpleDomainPlugin(
    name="RTK GNSS",
    detect_fn=detect,
    findings_fn=findings,
)

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
Register the plugin in your package pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."bagx.domains"]
rtk_gnss = "your_package.rtk_gnss:build_plugin"

The entry point may return:

  • a class instance implementing the DomainPlugin protocol, or
  • a zero-argument factory callable that returns one.

See examples/domains/rtk_gnss.py for a fuller reference implementation.

docs.title: Finding id policy
docs.text: Plugin display names are normalised into domain ids via bagx.findings.finding_id. Use lowercase dot-separated ids such as rtk_gnss.fix_rate.degraded so benchmark expected_findings contracts stay stable.

docs.title: Relationship to custom rules
docs.text:
• Domain plugins — stack detection and readiness findings tied to a framework (Nav2-like, RTK GNSS, agricultural robot, …).
  • Custom rules (bagx eval --rules) — topic/rate/latency checks for proprietary message stacks without writing Python.

Use both when you need framework-level findings and proprietary topic contracts.

docs.title: eval — Quality Evaluation
docs.text: Evaluate a single bag and produce a composite quality score (0–100).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx eval recording.db3
bagx eval recording.db3 --json report.json
bagx eval recording.db3 --rules warehouse_bot
bagx eval recording.db3 --findings-only
bagx eval recording.db3 --severity-min warning
bagx eval recording.db3 --findings-only --severity-min error
bagx eval recording.db3 --include-anomaly       # also merge fix-lost / spike segments
bagx eval recording.db3 --badge badge.json      # emit a shields.io readiness badge
bagx eval recording.db3 --tune fast_lio          # write FAST-LIO starting-point yaml
bagx eval recording.db3 --tune kiss_icp -o cfg/ # write cfg/kiss_icp_tuned.yaml
bagx tune --list                                # list supported frameworks
bagx eval recording.db3 --html report.html      # self-contained visual report
bagx report report.json --html report.html      # convert saved JSON to HTML

--html writes a single offline-friendly HTML file (inline CSS + SVG, no CDN). Use it for Slack/email attachments or as a shareable readiness snapshot. Temporal findings with time_range appear as colored bands on the topic timeline.

docs.title: Output filtering
docs.text:
• --findings-only skips the sensor-quality tables and recommendations and prints the structured findings list instead.
  • --severity-min {info|warning|error|critical} filters the findings list to that severity or higher. Applied to both the --findings-only text view and the --json payload.
  • --include-anomaly also runs anomaly detection and merges the resulting temporal findings (with time_range) into the report. Useful when the eval output is destined for bagx diff or bagx benchmark CI gates. Off by default because it re-reads the bag.

docs.title: Readiness badge
docs.text:
--badge <file> writes a shields.io endpoint JSON payload built from the composite score:

{ "schemaVersion": 1, "label": "Nav2 readiness", "message": "76.6/100", "color": "green" }
  • The label folds in the detected stack (Nav2 readiness, Autoware readiness, ...), or bag readiness when no domain is detected. Override it with --badge-label.
  • The colour tracks the overall score: brightgreen ≥ 85, green ≥ 70, yellow ≥ 50, orange ≥ 30, red below.

Host the file somewhere reachable by URL and reference it from a README:

![bag readiness](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://example.com/badge.json)

--badge composes with --json; both files are written in one eval run.

docs.title: GNSS Quality
docs.text:
• Fix rate: Percentage of messages with valid fix (status ≥ 0)
  • HDOP: Horizontal dilution of precision from position covariance
  • Altitude: Mean and standard deviation

docs.title: IMU Quality
docs.text:
• Noise: Estimated via first-order differencing — mathematically equivalent to Allan Deviation at τ=dt (one sample interval). This removes low-frequency vehicle dynamics and isolates sensor noise, even during motion.
  • Bias stability: Standard deviation of windowed means — approximates Allan Deviation at longer τ values
  • Frequency: Measured from message timestamps

Multi-IMU handling

If a bag contains multiple IMU topics, each is evaluated independently. The best-scoring IMU is reported.

Relationship to Allan Variance

The noise values reported by bagx are std(diff(x)) / √2, which equals the Allan Deviation at τ = 1/fs (sampling period). This was verified on real IMU data (Livox MID-360, 200Hz): diff-based = 0.0114 m/s², Allan σ(τ=dt) = 0.0114 m/s². For the standard Allan VRW/ARW specification (at τ=1s), use a dedicated Allan Variance tool on static data.

docs.title: Topic Sync
docs.text:
• Mean/max delay: for each message of the sparser topic in a pair, the record-time distance to the nearest message of the denser topic (e.g. each LiDAR scan → nearest IMU sample). Walking the denser topic would measure the sparser topic's period instead.
  • Evaluates the first 5 adjacent topic pairs by name order, among sensor streams (Imu, NavSatFix, LaserScan, PointCloud2, Image, …; camera_info, temperature and magnetometer topics are skipped)
  • Uses record time, so a constant offset hidden in header.stamp is not visible here; the TF clock check (tf.clock_mismatch.*) compares stamps against record time

docs.title: Pipeline latency
docs.text:
For stack pipelines (Nav2 scan → costmap, odom → localization; Autoware sensing → perception → planning → control; MoveIt joint_states → planned_path):

  • Exact when the output carries the header stamp of the input it was computed from (stamp propagation): latency = output record time − record time of the input with the same stamp. Used when ≥ 50% of outputs match; the recommendation ends with (header-stamp matched).
  • Approximate otherwise: delay from the latest input before each output, based on record times. This is accurate only for same-rate stages with a fixed offset, and under-reports when the latency exceeds the input period.

docs.title: Overall Score
docs.text: Weighted average of available component scores (GNSS, IMU, Sync).

docs.title: TF tree and message content
docs.text:
These checks add findings and recommendations but do not change the score.

  • TF tree (tf.*, category tf_tree, TF: prefix): see tf.
  • Message content (msg.*, category message_content, Data: prefix). These work without ROS: the SQLite fallback parses LaserScan / CameraInfo / Image / CompressedImage / JointState from CDR.
Finding id Severity Meaning msg.scan_no_valid_ranges.<topic> error Every scan has zero returns within [range_min, range_max] msg.scan_low_valid_ranges.<topic> warning On average < 50% of returns are within range msg.scan_config.<topic> error angle_increment == 0 or range_max <= range_min msg.scan_beam_count_changes.<topic> warning Beam count changes during the bag (two publishers, driver restart) msg.camera_uncalibrated.<topic> warning camera_info has an empty intrinsic matrix K msg.camera_info_zero_size.<topic> warning camera_info width or height is 0 msg.camera_info_size_mismatch.<topic> warning camera_info size differs from the Image in the same namespace msg.image_size_mismatch.<topic> error Image data length != step × height (truncated or mislabelled) msg.image_format_changes.<topic> warning Resolution or encoding changes during the bag msg.joint_state_name_set_changes.<topic> warning Different joint sets on one topic (several publishers) msg.joint_state_length_mismatch.<topic> error position length != name length msg.joint_state_nan.<topic> warning NaN joint positions msg.empty_frame_id.<topic> warning Scan / camera_info / image with an empty header.frame_id

docs.title: Structured findings
docs.text:
bagx eval --json includes a machine-readable findings array alongside the human-facing recommendations. Findings are the recommended surface for CI gating, benchmark expectations, and cross-release diffing — they have stable ids and never depend on recommendation text.

{
  "id": "sync.delay.high",
  "title": "Sensor sync delay is high",
  "severity": "warning",
  "category": "sync_quality",
  "domain": "slam",
  "affected_topics": ["/imu", "/lidar"],
  "evidence": [
    {"metric": "mean_delay_ms", "observed": 25.6, "expected": "<20", "unit": "ms", "topic": null}
  ],
  "suggested_action": "Enable deskew or timestamp compensation for tightly-coupled fusion.",
  "confidence": "medium"
}

docs.title: Field schema
docs.text: Field Type Notes id string Stable lowercase id, dot-separated (<domain>.<area>.<qualifier>). title string One-line human label. severity info / warning / error / critical See severity policy below. category string Coarse grouping (domain_detection, sensor_quality, topic_presence, rate_quality, sync_quality, workflow_observability, workflow_outcome, custom_rules). domain string | null slam / nav2 / autoware / moveit / perception / robotarm or a custom domain id. affected_topics string[] Topics this finding refers to. evidence object[] Measured facts: metric, observed, optional expected, unit, topic. suggested_action string | null Recommended next step. confidence low / medium / high Defaults to medium. time_range object | null Optional {start_ns, end_ns} (absolute ROS time) for findings scoped to a sub-interval of the bag — see Temporal findings.

docs.title: Severity policy
docs.text:
• info — readiness signal is healthy or merely informational.
  • warning — readiness is degraded but the bag is still usable; user action recommended.
  • error — readiness is unreliable; the bag should not be used as-is.
  • critical — reserved for catastrophic readiness loss (e.g. a mandatory topic missing on a safety-critical pipeline). Not emitted by built-in checks today; reserved for downstream plugins.

docs.title: Id naming convention
docs.text:
Ids follow <domain>.<area>.<qualifier> where the qualifier encodes the observed state, so passing states are also benchmark-checkable:

  • gnss.fix_rate.{good,gappy,unreliable}
  • imu.accel_noise.{good,noisy}, imu.gyro_noise.{good,noisy}, imu.rate.low
  • sync.delay.{good,high}
  • nav2.detected, nav2.odometry.rate_low, nav2.scan.rate_low, nav2.cmd_vel.rate_low
  • nav2.missing_cmd_vel, nav2.missing_global_plan, nav2.missing_navigate_to_pose
  • gnss.missing, imu.missing, gnss.hdop.high
  • custom.<domain_id>.evaluated
  • custom.<domain_id>.<label_token>.{pass,fail,skipped} — one per custom check
  • workflow.<topic_token>.{action_failures,result_failures,missing_service_responses}

Use these ids in benchmark manifests via expected_findings.

docs.title: JSON Schema
docs.text:
bagx ships a JSON Schema describing the Finding object at bagx/schema/findings.schema.json (Draft 2020-12). Locate it from Python:

from bagx.contracts import findings_schema_path, findings_schema

print(findings_schema_path())   # absolute path to the .json file
schema = findings_schema()       # parsed dict, cached

Use it from external tools (Grafana, Slack bots, GitHub Actions) to validate finding payloads without depending on bagx's Python runtime.

docs.title: Temporal findings
docs.text:
A finding may carry a time_range object that scopes it to a sub-interval of the bag. When --include-anomaly is set, the anomaly engine aggregates raw events into temporal findings:

  • anomaly.gnss.fix_lost.<topic> — segment from drop to recovery (or bag end if no recovery). Evidence includes duration_sec and recovered.
  • anomaly.imu.accel_spike.<topic> / anomaly.imu.gyro_spike.<topic> — clusters of spike events within a 30 s window.
  • anomaly.imu.frequency_drop.<topic> / anomaly.rate.gap.<topic> — message gap spans.
{
  "id": "anomaly.gnss.fix_lost.gnss",
  "title": "GNSS fix lost on /gnss",
  "severity": "warning",
  "category": "sensor_quality",
  "affected_topics": ["/gnss"],
  "time_range": {"start_ns": 1700000009000000000, "end_ns": 1700000009900000000},
  "evidence": [
    {"metric": "duration_sec", "observed": 0.9, "unit": "s", "topic": "/gnss"},
    {"metric": "recovered", "observed": false, "topic": "/gnss"}
  ]
}

bagx diff matches temporal findings segment-by-segment by time_range overlap, and bagx benchmark accepts a time_range_overlap constraint — see diff and benchmark.

docs.title: Custom message stacks
docs.text:
If your bag uses custom messages, you can still layer in domain-specific checks with --rules.

bagx does not need to decode those payloads for this mode. The rule engine works from:

  • topic names
  • topic types
  • message rates
  • timestamp-based latency between topics

The --rules argument accepts either a JSON file path or a plugin name from bagx rules list.

See custom-rules — Custom Message Rules for the rule format.

docs.title: Customizing thresholds
docs.text:
Via the Python API, you can tune scoring with EvalConfig:

from bagx.eval import EvalConfig, evaluate_bag

config = EvalConfig(
    gnss_fix_weight=0.6,
    gnss_hdop_weight=0.4,
    imu_accel_noise_excellent=0.05,   # m/s²
    imu_accel_noise_scale=200.0,
    imu_gyro_noise_excellent=0.005,   # rad/s
    imu_gyro_noise_scale=2000.0,
    sync_delay_excellent_ms=5.0,
    sync_delay_scale=1.5,
)

report = evaluate_bag("recording.db3", config=config)
print(report.overall_score)

docs.title: export — Data Export
docs.text: Export bag data to AI/analytics-friendly formats.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
# Parquet (default)
bagx export recording.db3

# JSON format
bagx export recording.db3 --format json

# AI-friendly mode (relative timestamps)
bagx export recording.db3 --ai --format parquet

# Specific topics only
bagx export recording.db3 --topics /gnss,/imu

# Custom output directory
bagx export recording.db3 --output ./my_export

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Description --format, -f parquet (default) or json --output, -o Output directory (default: ./export) --topics, -t Comma-separated topic filter --ai Relative timestamps from bag start --flatten / --no-flatten Flatten nested fields (default: flatten)

docs.title: AI mode
docs.text: With --ai, timestamps are normalized to seconds from bag start (first message = 0.0). This is useful for ML pipelines where absolute epoch timestamps are not needed.

docs.title: Output structure
docs.text:
One file per topic:

export/
  gnss.parquet          # /gnss topic
  imu.parquet           # /imu topic
  ouster_points.parquet # /ouster/points topic

Each file contains columns: timestamp_sec, timestamp_ns, plus flattened message fields.

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text: Use bagx-action to run bagx in CI without hand-writing workflow steps.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
- uses: rsasaki0109/bagx-action@v1

The action is a thin composite wrapper: install bagx from PyPI, then call the CLI.

docs.title: Benchmark gate
docs.text:
- uses: rsasaki0109/bagx-action@v1
  with:
    suite: benchmarks/my_suite.json
    fail-on: warning

See benchmark for manifest format.

docs.title: PR readiness diff
docs.text:
On pull requests the action:

  1. Runs bagx eval on the configured bag
  2. Restores a baseline eval JSON from actions/cache (keyed on the PR base SHA)
  3. Runs bagx diff --format markdown and posts a sticky PR comment
  4. Fails when --exit-on severity is reached

Prime the cache on main:

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  prime:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: rsasaki0109/bagx-action@v1
        with:
          bags: bag/recording.db3
          comment: "false"
      - run: cp .bagx-action/current.json .bagx-action/baseline.json
      - uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: .bagx-action/baseline.json
          key: bagx-eval-baseline-${{ github.sha }}

docs.title: Static HTML in CI
docs.text:
Combine with bagx eval --html in a custom step, or convert a saved JSON report:

- run: bagx eval bag.db3 --json report.json --html report.html
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: bagx-report
    path: report.html

docs.title: Workflow templates
docs.text: Older copy-paste templates live under examples/github_actions/ in the bagx repo. Prefer bagx-action for new workflows.

docs.title: Dogfooding
docs.text: The bagx repository runs bagx-action in .github/workflows/bagx-action-smoke.yml against a synthetic benchmark suite generated by scripts/prepare_ci_benchmark.py.

docs.title: mcp — MCP Server
docs.text:
Expose bagx analysis to LLM agents (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) via the Model Context Protocol.

Unlike bagx ask, no LLM API key is required. bagx returns structured JSON; the host agent does the reasoning.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: pip install bagx[mcp]

docs.title: Start the server
docs.text:
bagx mcp

This speaks MCP over stdio (default for local agent integrations).

docs.title: Tools
docs.text: Tool Description eval_bag(path) Quality eval → overall score, findings, recommendations list_topics(path) Topic names, types, counts, bag duration detect_anomalies(path, topic?) GNSS/IMU/rate anomaly report check_tf(path, required_frames?) TF tree edges + findings (multiple parents, gaps, clock mismatches, missing frames) compare_bags(path_a, path_b) Side-by-side metric comparison query_messages(path, topic, start_ns?, end_ns?, limit?) Decoded messages for one topic

docs.title: Claude Code
docs.text:
claude mcp add bagx -- bagx mcp

Or add manually to .mcp.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bagx": {
      "command": "bagx",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Use the full path to bagx if it is not on PATH inside Claude Code.

docs.title: Claude Desktop
docs.text:
Edit claude_desktop_config.json:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bagx": {
      "command": "bagx",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

macOS config path: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

docs.title: Example agent workflow
docs.text:
1. list_topics — discover /imu, /scan, /odom
  2. eval_bag — get readiness score and domain recommendations
  3. detect_anomalies — find IMU spikes or GNSS fix loss
  4. query_messages — inspect decoded fields around a suspect timestamp

docs.title: ROS1 bags
docs.text:
Install ROS1 reader support alongside MCP:

pip install bagx[mcp,ros1]

Then point tools at .bag files the same way as .db3 / MCAP directories.

docs.title: scenario — Scene Extraction
docs.text: Identify and extract time segments where notable or dangerous scenarios occur.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx scenario recording.db3
bagx scenario recording.db3 --json scenarios.json

docs.title: Detection rules
docs.text: Rule Trigger Default threshold gnss_lost Consecutive no-fix messages > 2.0 seconds sensor_dropout Topic stops publishing > 2.0 seconds high_dynamics IMU acceleration magnitude > 15.0 m/s² sync_degraded Sustained inter-topic delay > 100 ms

docs.title: Python API with custom thresholds
docs.text:
from bagx.scenario import detect_scenarios

report = detect_scenarios(
    "recording.db3",
    gnss_lost_threshold_sec=5.0,      # more tolerant
    accel_threshold_mps2=20.0,        # higher threshold
    dropout_threshold_sec=1.0,        # more sensitive
)

docs.title: scene — 3D State Extraction
docs.text: Extract position, orientation, and velocity time series from a bag.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx scene recording.db3
bagx scene recording.db3 --csv trajectory.csv
bagx scene recording.db3 --json scene.json
bagx scene recording.db3 --topics /odom,/imu

docs.title: Auto-detected message types
docs.text: Type Extracted fields sensor_msgs/NavSatFix Position (lat, lon, alt) sensor_msgs/Imu Orientation, angular velocity, acceleration geometry_msgs/PoseStamped Position, orientation geometry_msgs/PoseWithCovarianceStamped Position, orientation nav_msgs/Odometry Position, orientation, linear/angular velocity tf2_msgs/TFMessage Position, orientation (from transforms)

docs.title: CSV output columns
docs.text:
timestamp, pos_x, pos_y, pos_z, ori_x, ori_y, ori_z, ori_w,
vel_x, vel_y, vel_z, ang_vel_x, ang_vel_y, ang_vel_z,
accel_x, accel_y, accel_z, source

Fields are None when not available from the source topic.

docs.title: sync — Sync Analysis
docs.text: Analyze time synchronization between two topics.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx sync recording.db3 /camera /lidar
bagx sync recording.db3 /imu /gnss --json sync.json

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
For each message in topic A, finds the nearest timestamp in topic B:

Metric Description Mean delay Average nearest-neighbor delay (ms) Max delay Worst-case delay (ms) Median delay 50th percentile (ms) P95 delay 95th percentile (ms) Std Standard deviation (ms) Outlier rate Fraction of delays > mean + 3σ

docs.title: Interpreting results
docs.text: Mean delay Quality < 5 ms Excellent — suitable for tight sensor fusion 5–20 ms Good — suitable for most SLAM applications 20–50 ms Fair — may need timestamp compensation > 50 ms Poor — investigate clock sync or hardware triggers

docs.title: tf — TF Tree Validation
docs.text: Rebuild the TF tree from /tf and /tf_static and check that it can actually be used for replay: one parent per frame, no cycles, one connected tree, no pauses, and header stamps on the same clock as the sensors.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
bagx tf recording.db3
bagx tf recording.db3 --json tf.json
bagx tf recording.db3 --require-frames map,odom,base_link --fail-on error   # CI gate

bagx eval runs the same checks in its single read pass. TF findings appear in findings (category tf_tree), warnings and errors are listed under Recommendations with a TF: prefix, and the tree summary is saved in the tf key of the JSON report. TF findings do not change the readiness score.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text: Finding id Severity Meaning tf.multiple_parents.<frame> error A frame is published with two different parents. tf2 keeps one, so lookups flip between branches tf.cycle error The parent → child graph contains a loop tf.disconnected warning The frames form more than one tree, so frames in different trees cannot be looked up against each other tf.static_dynamic_conflict.<parent>.<child> warning The same transform is on both /tf and /tf_static tf.edge_gap.<parent>.<child> warning A dynamic transform paused longer than max(0.5 s, 5× its normal interval). Edges that pause together (one publisher) are grouped into one finding with a time_range tf.edge_stopped.<parent>.<child> warning A dynamic transform stops ≥ 2 s before the bag ends tf.zero_stamp.<parent>.<child> warning Dynamic transforms with header.stamp == 0 tf.stamp_regression.<parent>.<child> warning Header stamps go backwards (two publishers or a clock reset) tf.clock_mismatch.<topic> warning One topic's header stamps use a different clock from the rest (> 1 s off) tf.clock_split warning Stamped topics split into equally sized groups on different clocks tf.frame_missing.<frame> warning A sensor's header.frame_id never appears in the TF tree tf.required_frame_missing.<frame> error --require-frames names a frame that is not in the bag tf.required_chain_broken.<a>.<b> error Two consecutive --require-frames entries are in different trees tf.not_recorded info / error No TF at all, while ≥ 2 sensor frames exist (error when --require-frames is set)

docs.title: How the clock check works
docs.text: For every stamped topic (each TF topic and each sensor topic), bagx takes the median of header.stamp − record time. Topics whose offsets are within 1 s of each other are grouped. The largest group is treated as the reference clock, and every other topic is reported. This catches drivers that stamp with device time, GNSS/INS units that stamp with GPS time-of-week, and use_sim_time mismatches.

docs.title: Real-data examples
docs.text: Bag What bagx found Autoware all-sensors-bag4 ned → POS_REF is a separate tree, and /gnss/fix + /tf are stamped ~478,519 s (GPS time-of-week) while IMU/LiDAR use Unix time NVIDIA r2b_galileo / whitetunnel Every *_optical camera frame has two parents (static from the camera link, dynamic from the stereo node); /front_stereo_imu/imu stamps ~40 s off; segway_imu is not in the tree NVIDIA r2b_robotarm All six arm joint transforms pause together for 5.2 s; /tf stamps are 3 s behind the camera stamps

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from bagx.tf_tree import analyze_tf

report = analyze_tf("recording.db3", required_frames=["map", "odom", "base_link"])
print(report.roots, len(report.edges))
for finding in report.findings:
    print(finding.severity, finding.id, finding.title)

docs.title: Versioning and compatibility
docs.text: bagx is used as a CI gate, so its outputs are a contract. This page defines what counts as a breaking change and how changes are announced.

docs.title: What is covered
docs.text:
Surface Examples CLI Command names, option names, exit codes (--exit-on, --fail-on, benchmark failures) JSON reports Keys and types in eval / benchmark / diff / anomaly / tf JSON, schema_version Finding ids <domain>.<area>.<qualifier> ids, severity and category values Findings schema bagx/schema/findings.schema.json Python API bagx.eval.evaluate_bag, EvalReport / EvalConfig fields, bagx.reader.BagReader, bagx.tf_tree.analyze_tf, the domain plugin protocol, custom rule file format

Names that start with _ are internal and can change at any time. Some are re-exported for plugins (bagx.eval._select_topics); those follow the deprecation rule below.

docs.title: Version numbers
docs.text:
bagx uses MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

  • PATCH (0.6.0 → 0.6.1): bug fixes only. No new options, no removed keys. A fix may change a score or a finding when the old value was wrong; the changelog lists every such change under Fixed.
  • MINOR (0.6 → 0.7): new commands, options, findings or report keys. Before 1.0, a minor release may also remove or rename something, but only after the deprecation period below.
  • MAJOR (1.0 → 2.0): after 1.0, removals and renames happen only here.

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text:
1. The old name keeps working for at least one minor release and emits a DeprecationWarning (Python) or a warning line on stderr (CLI).
  2. The changelog lists it under Deprecated, with the replacement.
  3. It is removed in a later minor release (before 1.0) or the next major (after 1.0), listed under Removed.

Finding ids get the same treatment. A renamed id is emitted under both names for the deprecation period, so benchmark manifests and bagx diff baselines keep matching.

docs.title: Report schema_version
docs.text:
JSON reports carry their own schema_version, independent of the package version:

  • minor bump: additive changes (new keys, new finding categories). Consumers that ignore unknown keys keep working.
  • major bump: a key is removed or its type or meaning changes.

docs.title: Scores
docs.text: Readiness scores feed CI thresholds (min_overall_score), so any change to how a score is computed is called out in the changelog with the affected domains. Checks that only add findings and recommendations (TF tree, message content) are designed not to change scores.

docs.title: Supported environments
docs.text:
• Python: the versions in the CI matrix (currently 3.10–3.12).
  • ROS: works without ROS. With ROS 2, CI covers Humble and Jazzy through rosbag2_py.
  • Optional extras (mcap, ros1, mcp, llm) are pinned below the next major version once a breaking upstream release is seen (e.g. mcp<2).

docs.title: Why Autoware all-sensors-bag4 scores 83
docs.text: Overall: 82.8/100 · Domain: Autoware · ROS 2 · bagx 0.6.0

docs.title: This is not a "bad bag"
docs.text: The Leo Drive Isuzu all-sensors-bag4 is an official Autoware open-data recording (17.8 s, 17 topics, 9,489 messages). The Autoware domain checks pass almost entirely. What pulls the overall score down is the IMU sub-score (and, less, camera↔camera sync), not missing topics.

docs.title: Score breakdown
docs.text:
Overall is the mean of the sub-scores that apply to the bag:

Component Score Why GNSS 99.9 /gnss/fix has a 100% fix rate Domain (Autoware) 95.0 LiDAR at 9–10 Hz ✔, GNSS ✔; the three lucid_vision cameras run at 14 Hz, just under the 15 Hz perception target Sync 87.4 Camera↔camera pairs show 24–32 ms mean and up to 193 ms max offset; GNSS, IMU and LiDAR pairs stay under 4 ms mean IMU 48.8 Accel noise 0.43 m/s² (x axis 0.57), gyro y 0.048 rad/s Overall 82.8 (99.9 + 95.0 + 87.4 + 48.8) / 4

docs.title: Reading the IMU number
docs.text: bagx estimates noise as std(diff(x)) / √2. On a moving vehicle that number includes real vibration and road motion, not only sensor noise, so it is an upper bound. The bag is also too short (<60 s) and not static, so bagx cannot run Allan variance and says so. Treat the IMU warning as "do not take noise densities from this bag", not "the IMU is broken".

docs.title: Reading the sync number
docs.text:
bagx pairs each message of the sparser topic with the nearest message on the other topic. The three cameras are not hardware-triggered against each other, so 14 Hz cameras with free-running phase sit 24–32 ms apart on average. For multi-camera perception that is worth knowing; for LiDAR localization it does not matter (each concatenated pointcloud has an /sensing/imu/imu_data sample within 3.6 ms on average).

Before the unreleased sync fix, bagx walked whichever topic sorted first by name. For a dense/sparse pair that measured the sparse topic's period instead of the alignment, which put this bag's sync at 67.7 and its overall at 77.9.

docs.title: Planning / control
docs.text: bag4 is a sensing/localization bundle. bagx notes that planning/control topics are absent and skips those checks instead of penalizing them, which is why the domain score stays at 95.

docs.title: When to use this bag
docs.text:
• Sensor bring-up and LiDAR/GNSS localization regression tests
  • bagx regression on Autoware sensing detection
  • Not as a source of IMU noise parameters, and not as an end-to-end Autoware gate (use driving_20_kmh, 99.0, for that)

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
aws s3 sync s3://autoware-files/recordings/bags/2022-08-22_leo_drive_isuzu_bags/all-sensors-bag4_compressed/ ./all-sensors-bag4_compressed --no-sign-request
bagx eval all-sensors-bag4_compressed

See also the scoreboard.

docs.title: Why EuRoC MH_01_easy IMU looks noisy
docs.text: Overall: 60.3/100 · Domain: SLAM · ROS 1 · MAV handheld sequence

docs.title: The headline number
docs.text: EuRoC is a classic visual–inertial benchmark, but MH_01_easy scores only 60.3 overall because IMU quality lands at 23.1 while sync remains strong at 97.6.

docs.title: What drives the low IMU sub-score
docs.text:
bagx estimates IMU noise via std(diff(x))/√2 on accelerometer and gyro streams. On this bag:

  • Accelerometer noise is flagged at 0.79 m/s² — far above SLAM-oriented thresholds.
  • The platform is a flying MAV with aggressive motion; diff-based noise includes real dynamics.
  • EuRoC IMU units are older MEMS hardware; many LIO papers apply extra filtering anyway.

bagx therefore recommends LiDAR-only or LiDAR-forward odometry rather than tight LIO with default IMU weights.

docs.title: Why sync still scores well
docs.text: LiDAR and IMU timestamps are reasonably aligned (97.6 sync score). The recording is usable; the warning is about fusion strategy and IMU preprocessing, not a broken bag.

docs.title: Practical takeaway
docs.text: Goal Recommendation VIO / LIO benchmark Expect IMU tuning; compare against NTU VIRAL pattern LiDAR odometry only Reasonable candidate — sync is clean Default LIO noise model Not ideal without recalibration or denoising

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
pip install bagx[ros1]
export BAGX_SCOREBOARD_BAGS=/path/to/bags
bagx eval MH_01_easy.bag

Compare with TUM VI calib-imu1 (95.4 overall) for a calibration-grade reference.

docs.title: Why NTU VIRAL IMU looks noisy
docs.text: Overall: 84.0/100 · Domain: SLAM · ROS 1 · Drone platform · sequence eee_03 · bagx 0.6.0 + unreleased sync fix

docs.title: The headline number
docs.text:
NTU VIRAL is a multi-sensor drone dataset: two Ouster OS1 LiDARs, a stereo pair, a VN100 IMU, UWB ranging, DJI flight-controller GNSS/IMU, and Leica laser-tracker ground truth. On eee_03 (181 s, 19 topics, 389,804 messages) the time sync is clean and GNSS is present, so the score is pulled down by the IMU at 72.0.

Component Score Why GNSS 80.0 /dji_sdk/gps_position has a 100% fix rate; it carries no usable covariance, so the HDOP half of the score is a neutral 50 IMU (/imu/imu) 72.0 389 Hz; accel noise 0.16 / 0.37 / 0.35 m/s² (x/y/z), gyro 0.011 / 0.011 / 0.003 rad/s Sync 100.0 Every checked pair (DJI GNSS/IMU, VN100 IMU, left camera, OS1 node1 IMU/points) is within 2.4 ms mean Overall 84.0 (80.0 + 72.0 + 100.0) / 3

docs.title: What drives the low IMU sub-score
docs.text:
bagx estimates IMU noise via std(diff(x))/√2. On a flying platform that number includes real high-frequency motion and airframe vibration, not only sensor noise, so it is an upper bound. The accel average (0.30 m/s²) is above the threshold bagx uses for tightly coupled LIO, while the gyro (0.0085 rad/s) is fine.

bagx therefore recommends LiDAR-only or LiDAR-forward odometry (e.g. KISS-ICP), or LIO with a deliberately inflated accelerometer noise and some IMU pre-filtering, rather than default LIO weights. The bag is not static, so Allan variance is not computed; take noise densities from the dataset's imu_v100.yaml calibration, not from this flight.

docs.title: Why sync scores 100
docs.text: bagx pairs each message of the sparser topic with the nearest message of the denser one. Every LiDAR scan and camera frame has an IMU sample within a few milliseconds, which is what LiDAR–IMU and visual–inertial pipelines need.

docs.title: Practical takeaway
docs.text: Goal Recommendation LiDAR odometry benchmark Good candidate — sync is clean LIO with default IMU weights Expect tuning; inflate accel noise or pre-filter VIO with raw IMU Use the provided IMU calibration, not diff-based noise from flight

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
curl -L -o eee_03.zip https://researchdata.ntu.edu.sg/api/access/datafile/68132   # 2.0 GB, DR-NTU, CC BY-NC 4.0
unzip eee_03.zip
pip install bagx[ros1]
bagx eval eee_03/eee_03.bag

Compare with the Livox MID-360 row (98.7 overall) for a ground-vehicle LiDAR+IMU bag with a quiet IMU.
